item.title: iOS 27.3 beta 1 arrives with a bigger Siri AI, Safari overhaul, and a redesigned Health app
item.description:
Apple seeded the first developer betas of iOS 27.3, iPadOS 27.3, macOS Golden Gate 27.3, watchOS 27.3, tvOS 27.3, and visionOS 27.3, and it's shaping up to be the biggest update to iOS 27 since launch. Siri AI gains a long list of new in-app and cross-app actions, Safari gets a vertical tabs layout and an adaptive dark mode for sites without one, and StandBy comes to iPhone 11 and newer with the iPhone Duo's revamped design.

The beta also reintroduces the redesigned Health app — pulled from the 27.2 release — with new Insights and Longevity tabs and AI-powered Personal Guidance, brings Apple Intelligence features to China for the first time, and adds Live Rewind and Siri Recap to Apple Watch. A public release is likely months away, but developers can test now.

Sources

  • MacRumors: Everything New in the iOS 27.3 Beta
  • AppleInsider News: First developer betas of iOS 27.3, macOS 27.3 arrive for testing
  • MacRumors: iOS 27.3 Adds Vertical Tabs and Adaptive Dark Mode to Safari
  • MacRumors: iOS 27.3 Beta Brings Back Apple's Redesigned Health App
  • MacRumors: watchOS 27.3 Brings Live Rewind and Siri Recap to Apple Watch

item.title: Apple opens Siri AI to all developers with new 'app skills'
item.description:
For the first time, any developer can integrate their app with Siri AI. A new Developer Preview in the 27.3 betas lets apps define 'app skills' that teach Siri how to carry out complex, multi-step actions — a big step beyond the small set of supported schemas the first Siri AI versions offered.

The preview is a sneak peek ahead of a customer launch in a few months, and it signals Apple's plan to make Siri a genuine platform for third-party services rather than a first-party-only assistant. Developers can start building and submitting integrations now, with the features shipping as part of iOS 27.3 and its companion releases.

Sources

  • Daring Fireball: Apple Begins Opening Siri AI to Developers
  • 9to5Mac: Developers can now create advanced ‘app skills’ for Siri AI

item.title: iPad mini (A20 Pro) reviews: a great little tablet, still stuck at 60Hz
item.description:
Reviews of the new iPad mini landed ahead of its Friday launch, and the verdict is broadly warm with one recurring complaint. Reviewers praise the OLED display, the new design, and the acoustic display that fires sound from the front panel — though some note you can feel the whole tablet vibrate at high volume, and the two color options are, in MKBHD's words, 'annoyingly, slightly not black and slightly not white.'

The sticking point is the screen's 60Hz refresh rate: no ProMotion, despite the OLED upgrade, which several reviewers call frustrating and hard to justify. Battery life, meanwhile, appears better than Apple claims. Overall, it's a modern multitasker that broadens the mini's appeal — just don't expect a buttery display.

Sources

  • Daring Fireball: MKBHD on the New A20 Pro iPad Mini

item.title: Apple posts record $114.5 billion quarter as iPhone sales climb
item.description:
Apple reported fourth-quarter 2026 revenue of $114.5 billion, a quarterly record that narrowly beat Wall Street's $113.4 billion consensus. iPhone revenue rose year over year to $57.58 billion — notably without the non-Pro iPhone, which has been a driver in China — and CEO John Ternus fronted the earnings call for the first time.

Analysts were broadly positive on the results, though commentary also noted that Apple's analyst calls have been scripted for decades, a point raised after criticism of Ternus reading from a script. The record quarter caps a year in which Apple's staggered iPhone release schedule appears to be paying off.

Sources

  • AppleInsider News: Analysts on AAPL: how observers feel about Apple's Q4 financials

item.title: Apple explicitly bans employees from trading on insider info in prediction markets
item.description:
Apple has updated its insider trading policy to explicitly prohibit employees and contractors from using confidential company information to bet on prediction markets. The markets, which skirt the legal definition of gambling, let users bet on everything from product colors to launch timing — exactly the kind of nonpublic detail Apple staff might know.

The move closes a gray area as prediction markets have gone mainstream in the US, and it puts Apple employees on notice that insider-trading rules apply to these platforms just as they do to the stock market.

Sources

  • AppleInsider News: Apple officially restricts employee participation in prediction markets
  • 9to5Mac: Apple now explicitly bans employees from using confidential information in prediction markets

item.title: Fitness+ goes to the gym with personalized Gym Strength plans
item.description:
Apple Fitness+ is expanding beyond home workouts with Gym Strength, a new feature in the iOS 27.3 beta that builds a four-week strength plan around your goals, experience, schedule, and available equipment. You pick workout days, body areas, and session length, and get exercise, rep, set, and load recommendations plus short trainer video demos.

Plans adapt week to week based on your progress, and Apple Watch wearers can log sessions from the wrist. It's Apple's most direct play yet for gym-goers, turning Fitness+ from a living-room service into a full training companion.

Sources

  • MacRumors: Apple Fitness+ Gets Gym Strength Plans in iOS 27.3
  • 9to5Mac: Apple announces Fitness+ Gym Strength program with personalized workout plans
  • AppleInsider News: Bulk up with Apple Fitness+ new Gym Strength workout planner

item.title: Apple Music adds Selfie Sing karaoke videos
item.description:
iOS 27.3 adds Selfie Sing to Apple Music: a karaoke mode that records you singing along while lyrics scroll on screen, with a dedicated Selfie Sing playlist to get started. It builds on Apple Music Sing, which already let you lower vocals and follow highlighted lyrics — now the performance itself is the point.

It's a small, fun feature rather than a platform shift, but it fits Apple's pattern of turning Music into a more social, participatory app, and it's the kind of thing likely to show up in a lot of group chats this holiday season.

Sources

  • AppleInsider News: Apple Music gaining new Selfie Sing video karaoke mode

item.title: 'Stick' season 2 premieres on Apple TV
item.description:
Owen Wilson's golf comedy 'Stick' is back: the first two episodes of season 2 are now streaming on Apple TV, with new episodes arriving each Wednesday. Wilson returns as Pryce Cahill, chasing a comeback while coaching up-and-comer Santi, alongside Rhea Seehorn and Timothy Olyphant.

It's one of Apple TV's lighter originals, and the weekly rollout gives subscribers a reason to keep coming back through the fall.

Sources

item.title: Apple posts a record $114.5 billion quarter in John Ternus's first earnings report as CEO
item.description:
Apple closed fiscal 2026 with a record fourth quarter: $114.5 billion in revenue, up 12% year over year, and $30.7 billion in profit. iPhone revenue jumped 17.5% to $57.6 billion — a record for the quarter even without a new standard iPhone model — while Mac revenue rose 23.7% and Services grew 9.8% to $31.6 billion. iPad fell 10.4% and Wearables dropped 7.9%.

It was the first earnings report under new CEO John Ternus, who took over from Tim Cook on September 1, and the first call to feature COO Sabih Khan alongside CFO Kevan Parekh. The results beat Wall Street expectations, though the stock still dipped in after-hours trading once the call ended — a familiar pattern for Apple, whose quarter was strong enough to top even the COVID-fueled 2020 holiday quarter.

item.title: The memory crisis dominates the call: costs still climbing, iPhone Duo shortages with no end in sight
item.description:
If one theme defined the earnings call, it was memory. Ternus called current memory pricing 'unprecedented,' warning costs rose in the September quarter and will be worse in December and beyond, squeezing margins alongside Siri AI spending. Apple dodged questions about further price hikes, and its inventory ballooned to $14.54 billion as it stockpiled components.

The iPhone Duo, Apple's first foldable, remains badly supply-constrained: Ternus told Reuters Apple 'isn't able to predict' when supply and demand will balance, and UBS data puts average buyer wait times at 89 days. Mac and iPad supplies will also stay tight through the holidays, so anyone eyeing a new iPad mini or MacBook Pro may face delays.

item.title: Apple forecasts its biggest quarter ever, spends a record $45.77 billion on R&D, and passes 2.5 billion active devices
item.description:
Despite the supply constraints, Apple told investors the December quarter should be the best revenue quarter in company history, with CFO Kevan Parekh pointing to as much as 10% year-over-year growth. The company also disclosed a record $45.77 billion in fiscal 2026 R&D spending, up 32%, and confirmed it has received most of its reciprocal-tariff refunds from the U.S. government.

Two scale milestones framed the call: Apple's installed base has passed 2.5 billion active devices, and Siri now handles more than 2.5 billion requests a day — the audience Ternus is betting on as the rebuilt Siri rolls out. The board kept the quarterly dividend unchanged at $0.27 per share.

item.title: Supreme Court won't hear Apple v. Epic until January 2027
item.description:
The U.S. Supreme Court has scheduled oral arguments in Apple's appeal in its long-running Epic Games case for January 2027, pushing the timeline back further even as battles in the lower courts continue. The appeal concerns the lower court's authority in the case, and the delay raises the possibility that Epic's remaining claims could be rendered moot before the justices ever weigh in. For now, the App Store status quo — and the litigation over it — grinds on into another year.

Sources

  • 9to5Mac: SCOTUS sets hearing date for Apple’s appeal in Epic Games case
  • AppleInsider News: Supreme Court won't hear Apple & Epic's case until January 2027

item.title: App Store to require 18+ ratings for dating apps and AI romantic companions
item.description:
Apple announced new App Store age-rating rules: starting November 16, developers must disclose whether their apps include real-world location sharing or dating and relationship features, including virtual companions that engage in romantic or sexual content. Apps with those features will require an 18+ age rating, with full disclosure required by January 2027.

The move extends Apple's self-reported age-rating system, introduced in 2025 to get ahead of tightening global age-gating regulations, and lands as regulators worldwide scrutinize both location sharing and AI companions aimed at younger users.

Sources

  • 9to5Mac: Apple to require 18+ age ratings for dating apps and AI romantic companions
  • MacRumors: Apple Requiring Developers to Disclose Location Sharing and Dating Features in Apps
  • AppleInsider News: Apps with dating & location sharing features must be disclosed by January 2027

item.title: Hundreds of AI apps with hidden deepfake tools slipped past App Store review
item.description:
An investigation published November 2 uncovered a network of more than 400 connected apps and web domains that presented themselves as harmless AI services — pet portraits, language lessons, fitness coaching — but could load tools for generating sexually explicit and violent deepfakes from uploaded photos. The apps, apparently created by a single Chinese organization, passed App Store and Google Play review by hiding the abusive features behind ordinary ones.

Apple has removed 19 of the apps so far. The episode is an embarrassing miss for App Store review and a reminder of how easily deepfake abuse tools can be disguised as mainstream AI apps.

Sources

  • AppleInsider News: Hundreds of AI apps were part of a network hiding sexually abusive deepfake tools
  • 9to5Mac: AI apps with hidden sexual and violent deepfake features made it into the App Store

item.title: Apple warned users in 99 countries of possible mercenary spyware attacks
item.description:
Apple recently sent threat notifications to users in 99 countries warning they may have been targeted by mercenary spyware, according to reports. German authorities are investigating claims that lawmakers and government officials were among those targeted. The notifications are Apple's standard warning for the kind of sophisticated, state-linked attacks that go far beyond ordinary malware — and the sheer breadth, 99 countries at once, underscores how widespread commercial spyware targeting has become.

Sources

  • 9to5Mac: Apple recently notified users in 99 countries of potential mercenary spyware attacks

item.title: HomeView Ultra details leak: a bigger, swiveling smart-home hub for 2027 — and the current HomeView may double as a security camera
item.description:
The Information reports Apple is developing a larger, robotic HomeView — dubbed 'HomeView Ultra' or 'HomeView Max' in rumors — with a 9-inch display on a swiveling arm, a design said to resemble the old iMac G4 or Pixar's lamp mascot. It's expected in 2027 or 2028, after the standard HomeView reaches homes next week.

Separately, code sleuths found strings in HomeView Software 27.2 suggesting the hub itself could serve as a HomeKit Secure Video camera, with modes for Off, Detect Activity, Stream, and Stream & Allow Recording, plus scheduling based on whether residents are home, away, or asleep — with privacy protections for household members.

Sources

item.title: Also from Apple: Affinity lands on iPad, tvOS 27.2 build drops ahead of the new Apple TV 4K, and iOS 27.2.1 is on the way
item.description:
Canva released Affinity for iPad, bringing its free all-in-one design app — vector, photo, and layout tools unified on desktop last year — to Apple's tablet with a new touch-first Sketch Studio for Apple Pencil. The desktop app has drawn more than seven million users since the relaunch.

Meanwhile, Apple shipped a new tvOS 27.2 build for the fourth-generation Apple TV 4K ahead of the new model's November 13 launch, and iOS 27.2.1 is showing up in logs as a minor bug-fix update, with the first iOS 27.3 beta expected as soon as tomorrow.

item.title: Three new iPads reportedly coming in early 2027
item.description:
Apple is reportedly preparing three new iPad models for the first half of 2027, with the remaining iPad updates in the lineup expected in the same window. Reports point to refreshed models across the range, though specifics on which tiers get the update — and what chips or features they gain — are still thin.

For buyers, the timing matters more than the details right now: if you're shopping for an iPad this holiday season, the next refresh cycle is only a few months out. Expect firmer rumors on models and specs as the launch window approaches.

Sources

item.title: Apple reportedly trimming the non-touch MacBook Pro lineup
item.description:
Apple is reportedly set to eliminate non-touch MacBook Pros other than the core 14-inch model, further consolidating a lineup that has grown crowded with overlapping configurations. The move would leave the entry 14-inch as the sole MacBook Pro without the higher-end display and feature set of its pricier siblings.

The practical effect is a simpler buying decision: fewer near-identical models to compare, with a clearer step-up from the base Pro to the full-fat versions. It's the kind of quiet lineup pruning Apple does between bigger redesigns, and it suggests the current Pro generation is settling into its final form.

Sources

  • AppleInsider News: Apple to eliminate non-touch MacBooks Pros other than core 14-inch model

item.title: What to expect from Apple's Q4 2026 results on November 2
item.description:
Apple reports its Q4 2026 results on November 2, closing out a fiscal year shaped by the iPhone launch cycle, Mac refreshes, and services growth. Analysts will be watching iPhone demand, Mac momentum after the M5 rollout, and how services and wearables performed heading into the holidays.

The call also sets the tone for the quarter that matters most: guidance for the holiday period will tell investors whether Apple expects the current product lineup to carry it through December. Expect the usual focus on Greater China, installed-base growth, and any color on AI-driven features.

Sources

  • AppleInsider News: What to expect from Apple's Q4 2026 results on November 2

item.title: HomeView ships with six-month-old software — and may gain security camera features
item.description:
Apple's HomeView is shipping with software roughly six months old, according to reports — an odd stumble for a new product launch that raises questions about how polished the out-of-box experience will be. Separately, HomeView can already behave like a HomeKit security camera, and further camera features may be on the way.

The combination is telling: the hardware's home-security potential looks real, but the stale software suggests the launch was rushed or supply-constrained. Early buyers should expect day-one updates to matter more than usual, and the camera angle is worth watching as Apple builds out the home story.

Sources

  • MacRumors: Apple's HomeView Ships With Six-Month-Old Software
  • AppleInsider News: HomeView can behave like a HomeKit security camera

item.title: Weekend deals: M5 MacBook Air $200 off, plus Watch, AirPods, and more
item.description:
Nearly every M5 MacBook Air configuration is $200 off on Amazon this weekend, one of the first meaningful discounts on Apple's newest laptop. The broader weekend sale also covers Apple Watch Ultra 4, AirTag 2, other MacBooks, and AirPods.

If you've been waiting for a reason to buy the M5 Air, this is it — early-cycle discounts on a just-launched Mac are rare, and the $200 cut applies across the range rather than a single clearance configuration. Check the specific model you want, as stock on popular configs tends to move fast during these sales.

Sources

  • MacRumors: Nearly Every M5 MacBook Air Now $200 Off on Amazon
  • 9to5Mac: Weekend Apple deals: Apple Watch Ultra 4, AirTag 2, MacBooks, AirPods, more

item.title: Apple publishes steps to fix the Apple Watch daylight saving bug
item.description:
Apple has published steps to fix a daylight saving time bug affecting Apple Watch, which surfaced around the clock change. The issue caused incorrect time display for some users, and Apple's guidance walks through the fix rather than requiring a repair or replacement.

It's a small, seasonal bug, but time errors on a watch you rely on for alarms and workouts are genuinely annoying — the published workaround should resolve it quickly. If your watch still shows the wrong time after following the steps, a restart and re-pair is the usual next move.

Sources

  • MacRumors: Apple Offers Steps to Fix Daylight Saving Time Bug on Apple Watch

item.title: Crime blotter: Apple Store looters in France got bricked iPhones
item.description:
Thieves who looted an Apple Store in France walked away with iPhones that were promptly bricked, rendering the stolen devices useless. Apple's activation lock and remote bricking turned the haul into expensive paperweights — the latest reminder that stealing display or retail iPhones rarely pays.

It's a satisfying coda to a familiar story: Apple's anti-theft measures keep tightening, and organized retail theft of iPhones increasingly yields nothing but a police report. The incident is also a useful warning to anyone tempted by a suspiciously cheap 'new' iPhone with no box or receipt.

Sources

  • AppleInsider News: Crime blotter: Apple Store looters in France got bricked iPhones

item.title: Last Week in AVP #141: big games running natively, and a Paris opera house in immersive video
item.description:
This week's Vision Pro roundup leads with major games — GTA V, Halo, Jak, and Minecraft — running natively on the headset, alongside news of 10 Vision Pro headsets in use, a look inside Paris's Palais Garnier, and Edinburgh in the Dark, a 15-minute immersive film.

The native-games angle is the one to watch: Vision Pro's gaming story has been slow to build, and well-known titles running natively rather than streamed or adapted would meaningfully change the headset's appeal. The immersive film and cultural pieces continue to show where Apple's headset shines today — presence and place, not just productivity.

Sources

  • Last week in Apple Vision Pro: Last Week in AVP #141: GTA V, Halo, Jak & Minecraft Running Natively on AVP, 10 Vision Pro headsets, inside the Palais Garnier in Paris, Edinburgh In The Dark a 15-minute Immersive Film and more!

item.title: How the touchscreen MacBook Pro and macOS 27 are built for touch
item.description:
Apple's first touchscreen MacBook Pro — with its PROLED XDR display — arrives with a wave of touch optimizations in macOS 27, codenamed Golden Gate. Some shipped earlier this year, but a new batch debuted alongside the hardware, covering how the interface responds to taps, gestures, and touch-first interactions on a Mac.

The reaction from one 9to5Mac writer is telling, though: after five years without a major MacBook Pro redesign, the new machine is impressive on its merits but not an instant must-buy. The touch screen is the headline, but for many existing owners it may not be enough to justify upgrading yet.

Sources

  • 9to5Mac: Here’s how the new MacBook Pro and macOS 27 are optimized for touch
  • 9to5Mac: MacBook Pro with PROLED XDR looks awesome, but I’m not rushing to upgrade

item.title: Apple Intelligence finally reaches China on November 4
item.description:
Two years after its 2024 debut, Apple Intelligence is finally coming to China. Apple confirmed that the first core features will roll out as an open beta from November 4, ending a long absence driven by China's regulatory requirements for AI features.

China is one of Apple's most important markets, and the delay put iPhones there at a disadvantage against local rivals with their own AI features. The beta's arrival — alongside strong iPhone 18 Pro sales in China — should help close that gap.

Sources

  • AppleInsider News: Two years later, Apple Intelligence makes its way to China

item.title: iPhone 18 Pro surges in China, offsetting declines elsewhere
item.description:
China is doing much of the heavy lifting for the iPhone 18 Pro launch, with sales up 29% in the first three weeks, according to Counterpoint Research. Combined global sales of the Pro models rose 3.1% over the equivalent launch period last year, even as U.S. sales fell 4% and Japan dropped 27%.

Counterpoint credits better initial supply in China and higher prices for competing Android flagships; in the U.S., buyers reportedly saw too few changes to upgrade. The takeaway: Apple's growth story this cycle is increasingly a China story.

Sources

  • MacRumors: iPhone 18 Pro Sales Surge in China, Offsetting Decline in U.S. and Japan

item.title: A closer tour of Apple's upcoming HomeView smart home hub
item.description:
Developer Steve Troughton-Smith has shared a detailed tour of the software on Apple's upcoming HomeView smart home hub, built from a virtualized version created by Guilherme Rambo. The walkthrough covers the home screen, Control Center, clock faces like Flow and Snoopy, and apps including Timers, Alarms, World Clock, and Settings.

Apple has already demoed HomeView to select press, but this is the closest look yet at how the hub will actually feel day to day. It paints a picture of a device closer to a wall-mounted iPad experience than a simple speaker with a screen.

Sources

  • MacRumors: Here's a New Tour of Apple's HomeView Software

item.title: New iPad mini's smaller battery, same battery life
item.description:
Apple's EU energy label for the new iPad mini reveals a 4,900 mAh battery — slightly smaller than the previous model's 5,034 mAh. Apple's battery-life estimates are identical for both models, so the more efficient A20 Pro chip appears to make up the difference, with the new OLED display helping further on darker content since individual pixels switch off.

It's a small detail, but it shows how efficiency gains are doing real work: a smaller battery, an OLED screen, and no loss in endurance.

Sources

  • MacRumors: Apple Reveals New iPad Mini's Battery Capacity

item.title: Weekend deals: M5 MacBook Pro at a record low, Watch Ultra 4 discounted
item.description:
Amazon is clearing out M5 MacBook Pro stock at $1,349.99 for the 14-inch model with a 10-core CPU and GPU, 16GB of memory, and 1TB of storage — a $649 cut and the lowest price on record. Separately, the Apple Watch Ultra 4 has dropped to $699.99 on Amazon, matching its all-time low after launching in September.

Both deals look like clearance and early-holiday pricing rather than permanent cuts, so they likely won't last past the weekend.

Sources

  • AppleInsider News: Apple's M5 MacBook Pro plunges to $1,349, lowest price on record
  • MacRumors: Apple Watch Ultra 4 Hits All-Time Low Price With Amazon's $99 Discount

item.title: Apple Maps now blurs NASA, Space Force, and Air Force bases
item.description:
Apple Maps has begun blurring NASA, Space Force, and Air Force installations, blocking views of fighters on tarmacs and rockets on launch pads that map enthusiasts used to zoom in on for fun. The change appears recent and unexplained.

Whether it's a policy shift, a government request, or a quiet precaution, it marks a notable change for a service that has long shown military sites in detail. Expect more scrutiny if the blurring spreads to other sensitive locations.

Sources

  • 9to5Mac: Apple Maps begins blurring NASA, Space Force, and Air Force bases

item.title: PSA: manually update your Synology NAS now
item.description:
Synology NAS owners should take their devices offline and update them manually as soon as possible, especially older units. The warning follows the discovery of vulnerabilities in PHP that prompted large parts of the internet to patch — and home NAS boxes with internet-facing services are exposed to the same flaws.

If your NAS runs any web-accessible service, don't wait for an automatic update. Patch now, and treat this as a reminder to keep NAS firmware on a regular update schedule.

Sources

  • AppleInsider News: PSA: Manually update your Synology NAS right now

item.title: iOS 27.3 beta arrives next week, bringing Apple Intelligence to China
item.description:
Apple took the unusual step of confirming its next beta schedule: the first iOS 27.3 developer beta lands Wednesday, November 4 (Tuesday, November 3 in the U.S.), with a public release in December. The update will finally enable Apple Intelligence features in China, including Writing Tools, Genmoji, Clean Up, Notification Summaries, Priority Notifications, Visual Intelligence, and Live Translation with AirPods.

Not everything is coming, though: Siri AI and Image Playground are excluded for now, and the features are limited to iPhone 15 Pro and newer until Apple gets approval for iPad, Mac, and other devices. It's a significant milestone — China is Apple's second-largest market, and Apple Intelligence has been absent there until now.

Sources

  • 9to5Mac: Apple confirms iOS 27.3 beta is coming next week with Apple Intelligence in China
  • MacRumors: iOS 27.3 Will Enable These Apple Intelligence Features in China
  • MacRumors: Apple Says iOS 27.3 Beta Coming Next Week

item.title: iPhone Duo display cracks prompt Apple guidance — and a Samsung taunt
item.description:
Apple sent a memo to its stores and authorized service providers this week with guidance on diagnosing and handling inner display cracks on the iPhone Duo, telling technicians to inspect affected units and repair or replace them under standard procedures. The memo itself suggests the issue is widespread enough to warrant official guidance, though Apple says it affects only a small number of units.

Samsung wasted no time piling on, launching a Canadian ad campaign mocking the bright line appearing on some Duo displays, with slogans like "Folding. We know a thing or eight" and a nudge to switch to the Galaxy Z Fold8. Meanwhile, one-week-later reviews remain broadly positive, calling the Duo a strong first foldable despite its imperfections.

Sources

  • MacRumors: Apple Alerts Stores to iPhone Duo's Display Cracking Issue
  • MacRumors: Samsung Mocks iPhone Duo Display Cracks in New Ad Campaign
  • MacRumors: iPhone Duo Review: One Week Later

item.title: iPhone demand lifts Apple back past Nvidia as the world's most valuable company
item.description:
Apple has retaken the top spot as the world's most valuable company, once again swapping places with Nvidia in a lead that has changed hands repeatedly. Apple's stock closed October 30 at $344.63, down on a rough week for tech stocks overall but holding up better than rivals thanks to iPhone demand and services strength.

The rise also reflects a wave of hardware releases plus the smooth CEO transition from Tim Cook to John Ternus. It's a reminder that, even amid an AI-chip boom, Apple's device and services engine still commands the market's biggest valuation.

Sources

  • AppleInsider News: iPhone demand sees Apple topple Nvidia as most valuable company, again

item.title: HomeView software 27.2 arrives ahead of the device's November 13 launch
item.description:
Apple released HomeView Software 27.2 two weeks ahead of the new device's November 13 launch, offering an early look at what's inside. The update includes 20 default wallpapers in light and dark variations, plus Control Center and other features that weren't fully detailed at the device's announcement earlier in October.

The early software drop gives prospective buyers a clearer picture of the HomeView experience before launch day, and the wallpapers are already available to download for the curious.

Sources

  • MacRumors: HomeView Software 27.2: Wallpapers, Control Center, and More
  • 9to5Mac: Download all 20 Apple HomeView wallpapers in light and dark mode here

item.title: More details emerge on the touch-screen MacBook Pro
item.description:
Hands-on reports from Apple's Los Angeles event continue to fill in details on the new 14- and 16-inch MacBook Pro models with touch-enabled OLED displays, announced Wednesday. The keyboard and trackpad remain the primary inputs, with touch as an additional option for gestures like scrolling, pinch-to-zoom, and dragging.

The PROLED XDR display offers up to 2,000 nits of peak HDR and SDR brightness, a 10,000,000:1 contrast ratio, and Adobe RGB support alongside P3. Daring Fireball also published a full pricing and configuration breakdown for the M6, M5 Pro, and M5 Max models ahead of its full review.

item.title: Apple acquires Ascend.io, an agentic AI data-engineering startup
item.description:
Apple has acquired Ascend.io, a California company that built technology to help businesses automate data collection and analysis, and more recently added AI agents to help engineers manage that data. The deal surfaced through a notice on the European Commission's website — under the Digital Markets Act, Apple must publicly report acquisitions above a certain size — and Ascend.io's own site says it is winding down operations.

The acquisition fits Apple's pattern of buying AI firms for specific capabilities rather than consumer products; this one appears aimed at improving Apple's internal data management, with the agentic angle hinting at how Apple wants engineers to work with data going forward.

item.title: HomePod mini 2 launches today with S10 chip and new colors
item.description:
The HomePod mini 2 is out today, with first pre-orders arriving and the speaker available at most Apple Stores worldwide. It costs $149 in the U.S. and comes in two-tone pink, green, and blue alongside white and midnight.

The big upgrade is the S10 chip, up from the S5 in the original, and Siri AI support is coming in a future software update — though requests involving personal context will require an Apple Intelligence-enabled iPhone or iPad. It's the first refresh of Apple's smallest speaker in years, and it arrives just as the smart-home lineup gets a new sibling in the upcoming HomeView.

item.title: Russia adds Apple to its state surveillance registry
item.description:
Russia's communications regulator Roskomnadzor listed Apple and Microsoft on October 2 as "organizers of information dissemination," a classification that carries obligations to preserve communications and make data available to Russian security agencies. The requirements cover correspondence and messages containing audio or video, plus information identifying users and recording transmissions.

The listing puts Apple in a difficult position: complying with data retention and disclosure demands in Russia, or facing restrictions in a market where it has already scaled back operations. It's the latest escalation in Russia's efforts to bring foreign tech platforms under its surveillance framework.

item.title: Rian Johnson's iPhone camera app shoots to No. 1 on the App Store
item.description:
Filmmaker Rian Johnson has launched Chromagraph Camera, an iPhone photography app built with his longtime cinematographer Steve Yedlin and programmer Eric Cameron, bringing the image-processing techniques from his Knives Out films to iPhone stills. The app climbed to No. 1 in Photo & Video on the U.S. App Store, and Johnson's announcement on X drew six million views.

It's a rare case of a Hollywood director shipping a genuinely technical photo tool rather than a branded filter pack — and its viral debut suggests plenty of iPhone photographers are curious about a cinematic look straight out of camera.

item.title: The first touchscreen Mac, one day later: touch can be switched off, and macOS is only starting to adapt
item.description:
A day after Apple unveiled its first touchscreen Mac, the details that matter most to skeptics are emerging — and they are reassuring. The new PROLED MacBook Pro includes an accessibility setting to turn touch input off entirely, plus an option for pinch-to-zoom across the interface, so nobody is forced into the new interaction model. When touch is on, macOS reshapes itself: menu bar items expand under a fingertip, window controls grow, and the Dynamic Island pulls down into a floating widget.

Apple says this is just the start of making macOS touch-friendly, and hardware chief John Ternus frames touch as an addition that must not make the Mac lesser in any way. The lineup now spans $1,999 to a fully loaded $14,549 (thanks to a new 16TB SSD option), and TrendForce expects up to 1.5 million OLED touchscreen MacBook Pros to ship in 2027. The message: touch is here, but the traditional Mac is not going anywhere.

item.title: New iPad mini: OLED without ProMotion, and Apple explains why
item.description:
The new iPad mini's OLED display is its headline upgrade, but one omission drew questions: no ProMotion, so refresh rate stays at 60Hz instead of up to 120Hz. In interviews, Apple's VP of hardware design David Pakula defended the choice, saying the OLED panel itself delivers the meaningful upgrade and that ProMotion remains exclusive to the iPad Pro among iPads for now. He also discussed the mini's thinner, lighter design and its Acoustic Display.

Separately, Xcode 27.2 quietly confirmed specs Apple never lists: the new iPad mini (A20 Pro) has 12GB of RAM, the same as the iPhone Duo, while the new Apple TV 4K (A19) has 8GB. With a memory-chip shortage pushing RAM prices up industry-wide, those figures are worth knowing — and they suggest Apple is not skimping on memory in its smallest devices.

item.title: Apple cuts App Store commission to 26% in Taiwan after regulator talks
item.description:
Apple will lower its standard App Store commission in Taiwan from 30% to 26% for in-app purchases and paid apps on iOS and iPadOS, effective October 31. The change follows discussions with the Taiwan Fair Trade Commission, and Apple framed it as reflecting its ongoing commitment to developers.

The cut is small — four percentage points — but it continues a pattern: regulators in individual markets are steadily chipping away at the 30% standard, with Japan having secured a similar outcome. For developers selling in Taiwan, it is a modest but real revenue improvement; for Apple, it is another sign that the global App Store fee structure is being renegotiated market by market rather than all at once.

item.title: Abandoned Popcorn Time updater left up to 350,000 Macs open to takeover
item.description:
If you installed Popcorn Time on a Mac years ago, part of it may still be running — and it could have handed attackers full control. Security researchers at Eye Research detailed how Time4Popcorn, an unofficial fork of the old torrent-streaming app, left behind a small updater that checked for updates on every boot, even for people who had not opened the app in years. The updater trusted whatever it downloaded and ran it with full system privileges.

Worse, the project was long abandoned, so its update infrastructure was effectively unguarded. Up to 350,000 Macs are estimated to have been exposed. The broader lesson: forgotten software with persistent background components is a real attack surface, and it is worth auditing old installs — especially anything that phones home at startup.

item.title: Russia orders Apple to hand over users' messages on demand
item.description:
Apple and Microsoft have been added to a Russian state surveillance registry that requires them to hand over users' text, video, and audio messages on request, without a legal process. WhatsApp and Telegram are already on the same list; it is unclear why Apple was only added now.

The move follows Russia's blocking of FaceTime in 2025 and continues the country's tightening control over private communications. Apple has not publicly commented on how it will respond, but the registry obligation sits in direct tension with the end-to-end encryption Apple markets for iMessage and FaceTime. For users in Russia, the practical question is what data Apple actually holds and can produce — and whether services get further restricted if Apple resists.

item.title: DoorDash to buy Instacart for $17 billion
item.description:
DoorDash announced a deal to buy grocery-delivery rival Instacart for $17 billion, at $65 a share — a 26% premium over Instacart's October 22 closing price. The consideration will be at least 75% cash, with shareholders able to choose cash or DoorDash stock. The deal has not yet closed and will face regulatory review.

For users, the immediate effect is one fewer independent delivery option on the iPhone: two of the biggest app-based delivery platforms would become one company. Consolidation in delivery has historically meant fewer promotions and less competitive pressure on fees, though DoorDash will argue the combination lets it compete more effectively against larger rivals. Expect scrutiny from regulators given how much of the US delivery market the merged company would control.

Work on iOS 27.3 is already underway, with the next major iPhone update expected on Apple's usual cadence. For Duo owners still learning their device, Multiview is one of the first features that genuinely justifies the foldable form factor rather than merely adapting to it.

item.title: Apple unveils its first touchscreen Mac: the OLED MacBook Pro
item.description:
Apple broke one of its longest-standing taboos, announcing 14- and 16-inch MacBook Pros with a touch-enabled PROLED XDR display — tandem OLED technology Apple calls the best display ever in a pro laptop, with up to 1,600 nits-class brightness, striking contrast, and vivid color. The machines run M5 Pro and M5 Max chips, are slightly thinner and lighter than the mini-LED models they sit alongside, and replace the notch with a Dynamic Island that hosts Live Activities, Spotlight, and Siri.

The nostalgia touches are real, too: the glowing Apple logo returns to the lid after a decade away, its brightness tied to the display. Touch costs nothing in battery life — up to 24 hours claimed — and CEO John Ternus told WIRED the Mac remains an indirect-input device first, with touch added only once it didn't make the machine heavier or thicker. Prices start at $2,899 (14-inch) and $3,399 (16-inch), with a fully maxed configuration topping $14,549. Pre-orders are open now; machines arrive November 6.

item.title: Apple vs. OpenAI trade-secrets trial set for July 2027
item.description:
Judge Edward Davila has set the schedule for Apple's trade-secrets lawsuit against OpenAI, two former Apple employees, and OpenAI's io Products hardware unit, with trial slated to begin July 19, 2027. The dispute, rooted in events going back to 2019, will by then have been in litigation for about a year.

The judge also granted Apple some of the OpenAI documents it had requested, a further win in the discovery fight ahead of trial. The case is one of the highest-stakes talent-and-technology disputes in AI hardware: Apple alleges its former employees misappropriated trade secrets on their way to building OpenAI's device efforts. With the date now fixed, both sides face a long runway of depositions and document exchanges before a courtroom showdown.

item.title: South Korea fines Apple $15.5 million, orders App Store payment changes
item.description:
South Korea's media regulator fined Apple 20.8 billion won ($15.5 million) and Google 42.9 billion won ($32 million), ordering both to change app payment policies the regulator says violate a 2021 law meant to open up alternatives. Apple and Google did allow third-party payments inside apps, but charged developers a 26% commission and restricted some features — conditions regulators said pushed developers back toward the companies' own systems.

The ruling requires Apple to let developers link to external payment options from their apps. It adds South Korea to the growing list of countries chipping away at the App Store's payment model, and it lands as Apple faces similar pressure in the EU and US. Neither company has said yet whether it will appeal, but the order itself is a concrete change developers in Korea can act on now.

item.title: Russia now requires Apple to store user communications for security agencies
item.description:
Apple and Microsoft are now subject to Russian regulations requiring companies to store users' communications and hand them over to security agencies on request, according to Bloomberg. The requirement marks a significant escalation in Russia's long-running pressure on foreign tech companies to make user data available domestically.

Details of exactly what data is covered and how Apple will comply remain thin, but the stakes are obvious: a company famed for encryption and privacy marketing now faces a legal obligation in Russia that sits in direct tension with that stance. Watch for whether Apple comments publicly, and for how the rule interacts with its existing practice of storing some Russian user data locally — a compromise that has drawn criticism from privacy advocates before.

item.title: iPhone Duo tipped to take nearly 30% of the foldable market in 2027
item.description:
Apple's foldable iPhone Duo could capture nearly 30% of the global foldable smartphone market by 2027, according to a new TrendForce report, riding strong early demand for the device. That would be a remarkable debut for a company entering a category Samsung and others have spent years building — and a sign that foldables may finally be moving from niche to mainstream once Apple throws its weight behind them.

The forecast matters beyond bragging rights: a 30% share would make Apple the foldable segment's pace-setter almost immediately, pressuring rivals on price, durability, and software. It also suggests Apple's supply chain is gearing up for volume, not a cautious limited run. The usual caveat applies — analyst forecasts this far out are directional, not guarantees — but the direction of travel is clear.

item.title: Memory crunch deepens: shortages through 2030 as Mac Studio's 512GB option lands at $22,299

Key Apple memory supplier SK Hynix warned that RAM and flash shortages are likely to last through at least 2030, keeping product prices high. Apple is reportedly one of 14 customers to have locked in priority orders, but those contracts don't shield against price increases driven by supply and demand — a warning that helps explain the creeping price hikes across Apple's lineup, including the MacBook Neo's shrinking education discount.

The same day, Apple finally opened orders for the long-promised 512GB RAM configuration of the M5 Ultra Mac Studio. The upgrade alone costs $15,500, pushing the minimum configuration to $22,299 — and to $29,799 with 16TB of storage. It's a halo machine for a tiny audience, but also a vivid price tag for the memory crunch: RAM is now the luxury option.
